thread:
incident-bot: PagerDuty triggered for inferpool-usw1 - multiple NotReady node flaps (gpu-307, gpu-308). Error rate spike and increased 5xxs. Paging oncall @maya. https://pagerduty.example/INC-1423

maya: I'm on it, paging into this thread. Starting quick triage.

devon: I'll pull metrics and logs — checking node status and recent evictions.

runtime-bot: Observed container restarts on pods infer-runtime-4/5. Last kernel/driver lines:
```
NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79
containerd: process exited with status 139
kubelet: OOM kill invoked for process 0x7ff
```

maya: `kubectl get nodes -o wide` shows gpu-307 and gpu-308 in NotReady (KubeletReady:false). Other nodes stay Ready.

devon: quick check of schedules — no maintenance windows. No recent kernel upgrades reported. Could be GPU driver crash loop.

leo: routing update: temporarily steer inference traffic away from region-usw1 via smart-routing policy -> prefer us-west-2 and dedicated pools. Doing a soft-failover now.

maya: cordoning gpu-307 (`kubectl cordon gpu-307`) and attempting drain. Drain hangs on pod infer-runtime-4 with terminating state. Logs show KV cache unmount timeout.

runtime-bot: Relevant runtime log excerpt:
```
[2026-03-17T10:15:12Z] runtime: kvcache: flush timeout waiting for lock
[2026-03-17T10:15:14Z] runtime: gpu-driver: reported Xid 79, process crash
[2026-03-17T10:15:20Z] runtime: container shutdown triggered, graceful timeout exceeded
```

devon: Scaling up spare capacity in other pools to absorb traffic: `kubectl scale deployment/infer-deployment --replicas=30 -n inference` (was 20).

maya: drain still blocked. Trying `kubectl delete pod infer-runtime-4 --force --grace-period=0` to force terminate.

leo: routing finished steering ~80% of trafic off usw1, small residual for sessions pinned to existing connections. Customer impact window estimated ~10-15 minutes.

ryan: Noted an increase in 5xxs around 10:14-10:26; p50 stable, p99 latency spiked ~900ms -> 1.8s and error rate +4% for hosted customers in region-usw1. Flagging support to notify customers with SLA watch.

maya: Forced pod deletion succeeded, node kubelet still flapping. Kubelet logs show repeated registration then disconnects. Command output:
```
Mar 17 10:16:32 kubelet[1234]: level=error msg="failed to heartbeat: context deadline exceeded"
Mar 17 10:16:35 kubelet[1234]: level=warn msg="restarting kubelet due to runtime response timeout"
```

devon: Since drain failing + kubelet instability, proposing node reboot (gpu-307) to reset driver state. Any objections?

leo: go for reboot. Keep routing in place.

maya: Rebooting gpu-307 now (`ssh ops@gpu-307 sudo systemctl reboot`). ETA ~3m.

runtime-bot: Noted GPU driver residue; kernel stack traces included Xid 79 and driver module unload timeouts. Could be memory leak in kvcache when a guest process OOMs.

devon: Initiating azure/gcp cloud instance reboot via cloud-console as fallback if kubelet doesn't recover.

maya: gpu-307 back to Ready at 10:20:48, kubelet re-registered, runtime pods rescheduled. Monitoring.

leo: routing policy now easing — keep small percentage (5%) routed to usw1 for verification.

ryan: Customer impact summary: ~7% of requests from region-usw1 saw elevated latencies/errors during the incident window. No large-scale data loss. Notifying top affected customers via support.

maya: gpu-308 still NotReady, repeating the same steps: cordon, force-delete stuck pods. Kernel/gpu-driver still showing Xid events.

devon: For gpu-308 trying a kubelet restart instead of full reboot to observe difference: `sudo systemctl restart kubelet`.

runtime-bot: After kubelet restart, pods remain stuck in crashloop with Xid 79. Suggest full node reboot for gpu-308 as well.

maya: Rebooting gpu-308 now.

leo: Keep traffic steering active until both nodes stable. Ops team: continue to hold autoscale limits to avoid overcommit.

maya: gpu-308 back to Ready at 10:38:12. Runtime pods returned healthy. Observability shows error rate dropping back to baseline by 10:42.

ryan: Rolling back routing - returning traffic to normal balancing over the next 5m.

devon: Post-incident quick notes: probable root cause = GPU driver/kernel state corruption triggered by specific workload pattern that caused OOM and Xid 79 (GPU page fault). KV cache in runtime aggravated pod termination, leading to drain hangs.

maya: Immediate mitigations applied:
- Steered traffic off region until nodes stable
- Forced pod deletion + node reboots to clear driver state
- Scaled other pools to absorb load

leo: Customer impact: limited to region-usw1, short-lived (10-30m), impacting latency/p99 and small error increase. Support already notified top 5 customers; status page updated.

maya: Follow-ups / action items:
- runtime team to add a faster fallback to skip KV cache flush on pod force-delete (assigned to devon)
- infra to enable node-level watchdog to auto-reboot on repeated Xid 79 (assigned to ryan)
- schedule deeper postmortem + kernel/driver debug (owners: runtime + infra)

runtime-bot: Temporary mitigation: added extra process to watch for Xid 79 and restart pods earlier in the chain. Will be reverted after proper fix.

devon: I'll open the postmortem doc and link details, logs, and commands.

maya: Thanks team — incident mitigated and routing normalized. Marking this thread closed; postmortem to follow. :white_check_mark:

leo: +1 :thumbsup:

incident-bot: PagerDuty INC-1423 acknowledged and resolved at 2026-03-17T10:45:10Z.
